title: Sebastian and the Songbook
premise: Ansel Galloway built a career orchestrating perfect weddings for other people while quietly burying their own ruined one—eleven years ago, a letter from their then-partner Marisol never arrived, and Ansel fled the life they'd built together. When a deceased client's estate yields a misdelivered letter and an old songbook the two once filled with lyrics, Ansel must track down Marisol, now a celebrated singer who turned their shared songs into fame. Reconciling means confronting the truth that Ansel's family never accepted them and that Marisol's silence was its own betrayal. In the end, Ansel stops hiding behind other people's happy days, forgives the person in the mirror, and chooses a second chance—not a rewind, but something new written together in the songbook's empty pages.
about_author: Tamsin Whitlock is a former wedding pianist who spent a decade watching love arrive on schedule before writing about the kind that doesn't. She lives in a coastal town full of chapels she has never once entered.

chapters.title: The Vow Machine
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel flawlessly executes the wedding of a socialite couple, hollow inside, then returns to an empty apartment where a lawyer's letter about the Delacroix estate waits unopened. Beat: competence as armor; loneliness beneath the polish.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Sorting the late Mrs. Delacroix's belongings, Ansel finds a misdelivered envelope addressed to them, postmarked the week everything fell apart. They don't open it. Beat: dread and magnetic pull; the past knocking.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At 3 a.m., Ansel reads Marisol's letter—an apology, an address, an invitation that expired a decade ago—and the old songbook tucked with it, half their handwriting inside. Beat: grief resurfacing; the wound named.

chapters.title: The Client Who Won't Say Yes
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. New client Priya keeps rejecting every venue, and Ansel realizes she's stalling for reasons of her own. Their sparring sessions become an odd friendship. Beat: found family seed planted; humor returning.

chapters.title: Marisol Vane, Live
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel hears Marisol's voice on a café radio—their stolen song on the charts—and learns she's headlining a hometown benefit. Beat: betrayal's fresh sting; the decision to go forms.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol, exhausted by fame and a controlling manager, confesses to her bandmate that she never stopped writing to a ghost. Beat: mirror chapter; her guilt and longing revealed.

chapters.title: Backstage Pass, Burned
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel gets backstage at the benefit, comes face to face with Marisol mid-interview, and walks out before she can finish saying their name. Beat: collision without resolution; pride vs. yearning.

chapters.title: The House That Sang
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel visits the crumbling house where they and Marisol once lived, remembering the family that disowned them and the songs that kept them alive. Beat: backstory excavation; understanding their own flight.

chapters.title: Priya's Confession
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya admits she's marrying to please a dying mother, not herself, and asks Ansel the question that guts them: 'Did you ever marry anyone you loved?' Beat: theme sharpened; Ansel forced toward honesty.

chapters.title: Second Verse
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol finds Ansel at the old house. They argue about the letter, the silence, the songs she took. She reveals she never knew why he vanished—her letters after that first one were returned. Beat: the misunderstanding surfaces; neither yields.

chapters.title: The Intermediary
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel discovers Marisol's manager intercepted everything, curating her past for the brand. Proof arrives in the Delacroix estate files—the manager's family and Mrs. Delacroix were entangled all along. Beat: villain identified; righteous anger.

chapters.title: Duet, Unrehearsed
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol and Ansel play the songbook together for the first time in eleven years, finishing an unfinished song, and nearly kiss before Marisol's manager calls. Beat: tenderness reignited; interruption as threat.

chapters.title: Contract Terms
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The manager offers Ansel a lucrative deal: plan Marisol's publicity wedding to a safe, marketable fiancé, or be painted as an unstable stalker from her past. Beat: power's corruption made personal; the trap closes.

chapters.title: The Mirror Test
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel drafts the acceptance email, then confronts their reflection and the years of self-erasure—changing their name, their voice, their wants. They delete the email. Beat: the forgiveness-of-self turn; quiet climax of character.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At the fake engagement's rehearsal dinner, Marisol publicly refuses the script, singing instead the unfinished duet—naming Ansel to a thousand strangers. Beat: public climax; love as declaration.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The manager retaliates—leaked contracts, a smear piece, Ansel's business frozen. Priya and her mother, and Marisol's band, rally around them. Beat: cost of courage; found family solidifies.

chapters.title: The Delacroix File
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, a journalist by training, uncovers the manager's forged letters and financial fraud in the estate records, handing Ansel the leverage. Beat: allies strike; power begins to shift.

chapters.title: What Ansel Galloway Wants
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel testifies at the estate hearing and, on record, tells the whole story—the disowning, the letter, the years invisible. Marisol watches from the gallery. Beat: identity reclaimed in public; catharsis.

chapters.title: The Empty Page
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Manager exposed and gone, Marisol asks Ansel not to resume what they were but to write something new. Ansel admits fear, not indifference, kept them away. Beat: honest reckoning; forgiveness exchanged.

chapters.title: A Wedding Worth Planning
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel plans Priya's small, true wedding—no spectacle—and realizes the work still means something when it's honest. Marisol helps fold the chairs. Beat: vocation healed; joy without irony.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol's benefit concert becomes a homecoming; she and Ansel perform the finished song, and afterward, on the old house's porch, they exchange not rings but a new page in the songbook. Beat: resolution; love chosen freely.

chapters.title: The Songbook, Continued
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A year later: Ansel's rebuilt business thrives, Priya is family, and the songbook's blank pages wait on the kitchen table beside two coffee cups. Ansel writes the first line of something new. Beat: peace earned; second chance accepted.
